title: Know, select and use materials, tools and equipment safely for technological purposes

lessons.title: Choosing the right material and tool
lessons.html:
Materials

Every job on a farm uses materials. A material is what something is made from. To make a good job, you must choose the right material for the purpose.

MaterialGood forWatch out
Wood (poles, planks)Fence posts, kraals, shelvesRots in wet soil unless treated
Steel and wireFences, gates, framesRusts; sharp ends cut skin
Plastic (PVC, polyethylene)Water pipes, drip lines, tanksGets brittle in the sun over time
Cement and bricksTroughs, floors, dip tanksWet cement burns skin

Hand tools

Hand tools work with your own strength: hammer, spade, pick, panga, saw, pliers, spanner, screwdriver and wire strainer. Power tools use electricity or fuel: drill, angle grinder, chainsaw and brush cutter.

Selecting the right tool

  1. Think about the job. For example, to cut fencing wire use wire cutters or pliers, not a panga.
  2. Pick the right size. A small spanner on a big nut will slip and hurt your hand.
  3. Check the tool before you use it. Look for loose handles, cracks, blunt edges and damaged cables.
  4. Do not use a broken tool. Put it aside and tell your supervisor.

Measuring

Many jobs need measuring first, using a tape measure, spirit level or measuring jug. Measure twice and cut once, so you do not waste material. Write down the measurements.

A tool used for the wrong job can break, damage the work and injure you or the people around you.

Ask an experienced worker or your supervisor if you are not sure which material or tool is right. It is better to ask than to waste material or get hurt.

lessons.title: Using tools and equipment safely
lessons.html:
Safety comes first

The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says your employer must give you safe tools and training, and you must work safely and use the protective equipment you are given.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)

  • Safety glasses or goggles when grinding, drilling, chopping or cutting wire.
  • Gloves when handling wire, cement, sharp material or chemicals.
  • Safety boots to protect your feet.
  • Ear protection near loud machines such as chainsaws and brush cutters.
  • Dust mask when cutting, sanding or mixing cement.

Safe working rules

  1. Only use power tools you have been trained and allowed to use.
  2. Keep your work area clean and tidy, so nobody trips.
  3. Keep other people, especially children, away from your work.
  4. Cut away from your body, never towards it.
  5. Switch off and unplug a power tool before you change a blade or clean it.
  6. Keep electrical cables away from water and sharp edges.
  7. Carry sharp tools with the blade pointing down, and never throw tools to someone.

Never do this

  • Never remove a guard from a machine.
  • Never use a tool when you are tired, drunk or have taken drugs.
  • Never use petrol to clean your hands or start a fire.

Looking after tools

After work, clean the tools, oil steel parts so they do not rust, sharpen blades, and store everything in the store room in its place. Count the tools so nothing gets lost. Report damaged tools.

If someone is hurt

Stop work, make the area safe, call for help and report the injury to your supervisor straight away. Only give first aid if you are trained.

Key points

  • Choose the right material and tool for each job.
  • Check tools before use and do not use broken tools.
  • Always wear the correct PPE.
  • Switch off and unplug power tools before cleaning or changing parts.
  • Clean, store and count tools after work.
